headline: Tanzid Tamim's century as Bangladesh take 153-run lead against Australia
summary: The Tigers dominate Day 2 in Darwin, recording their highest-ever Test total in Australia with 351-6.
details: Bangladesh dominated Australia throughout Day 2 of the first Test in Darwin, finishing the day at 351-6 with a commanding 153-run lead.
Tanzid Tamim starred with a spectacular maiden Test century, becoming the first Bangladesh batter to score a Test ton in Australia.
Skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto provided crucial support with a half-century, helping the team reach their highest-ever Test total on Australian soil.
Tanzid and Mominul Haque shared a 102-run second-wicket partnership, marking only the second century stand between the two teams in Australia.
Australia's Mitchell Starc took a wicket to reach 435 Test wickets, surpassing Kapil Dev to move into 11th place on the all-time list.
Steve Smith equalled Joe Root for the most catches by a fielder in Test history with 218 catches.
Former Australian legend Ricky Ponting warned that the Australian side will be nervous as Bangladesh continues to dictate terms.
caption:
A historic day for the Tigers! Tanzid Tamim becomes the first Bangladeshi to score a Test century in Australia.

Bangladesh dominated Australia throughout Day 2 of the first Test in Darwin, finishing the day at 351-6 with a commanding 153-run lead.

Tanzid Tamim starred with a spectacular maiden Test century, becoming the first Bangladesh batter to score a Test ton in Australia.

Skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto provided crucial support with a half-century, helping the team reach their highest-ever Test total on Australian soil.

Tanzid and Mominul Haque shared a 102-run second-wicket partnership, marking only the second century stand between the two teams in Australia.

Australia's Mitchell Starc took a wicket to reach 435 Test wickets, surpassing Kapil Dev to move into 11th place on the all-time list.

Steve Smith equalled Joe Root for the most catches by a fielder in Test history with 218 catches.

Former Australian legend Ricky Ponting warned that the Australian side will be nervous as Bangladesh continues to dictate terms.

headline: 9 workers killed by toxic gas at Sitakunda shipbreaking yard
summary: Workers were exposed to carbon monoxide while dismantling an LNG carrier; several victims died while attempting to rescue their colleagues.
details: Nine workers died after being exposed to toxic gas at Ferdous Steel Ship Recycling Industries in Sitakunda, Chattogram, on Monday morning.
The incident occurred while workers were cutting into the LNG carrier vessel MT Rasi. The gas, believed to be carbon monoxide, spread rapidly after coming into contact with water.
Several workers died while attempting to rescue their colleagues who had first fallen unconscious inside the ship.
One survivor, Mohammad Selim, described the intensity of the fumes, stating that another 20 seconds inside the ship would have killed him despite wearing a mask.
The victims include Motiur Rahaman (17), Palash Das, Sunny Das, Mohammad Khokon Mia, Mohammad Mansur, Abdul Alim Sujon, Md Rana, Nasir Uddin, and Md Hanif.
Chattogram DC Md Zahidul Islam Mian stated that the families of the deceased will receive Tk 10 lakh in financial compensation.
A team of chemists and the army are working to control the gas spread, and the DC confirmed that legal action will be taken if company negligence is found.
caption:
9 workers dead in Sitakunda. Some died while trying to save their colleagues from toxic fumes.

Nine workers died after being exposed to toxic gas at Ferdous Steel Ship Recycling Industries in Sitakunda, Chattogram, on Monday morning.

The incident occurred while workers were cutting into the LNG carrier vessel MT Rasi. The gas, believed to be carbon monoxide, spread rapidly after coming into contact with water.

Several workers died while attempting to rescue their colleagues who had first fallen unconscious inside the ship.

One survivor, Mohammad Selim, described the intensity of the fumes, stating that another 20 seconds inside the ship would have killed him despite wearing a mask.

The victims include Motiur Rahaman (17), Palash Das, Sunny Das, Mohammad Khokon Mia, Mohammad Mansur, Abdul Alim Sujon, Md Rana, Nasir Uddin, and Md Hanif.

Chattogram DC Md Zahidul Islam Mian stated that the families of the deceased will receive Tk 10 lakh in financial compensation.

A team of chemists and the army are working to control the gas spread, and the DC confirmed that legal action will be taken if company negligence is found.
